verses.source_sanskrit:
गणेशं मनसा ध्यात्वा सृष्टिं कर्तुं मनो दधे ।
आदौ तस्य विधेर्देहादविद्या सा विनिःसृता ॥१॥
verses.text: ಮುದ್ಗಲನು ಹೇಳಿದನು: ಗಣೇಶನನ್ನು ಮನಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಕಲ್ಪಿಸಿದನು. ಮೊದಲು ಆ ವಿಧಾತನ ದೇಹದಿಂದ ಅವಿದ್ಯೆಯು ಹೊರಹೊಮ್ಮಿತು. ॥೧॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
ಮುದ್ಗಲ ಉವಾಚ is the printed speaker heading before verse 1; included as narrative attribution.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Formal narrative preserves Mudgala’s printed speaker heading, Brahma’s mental meditation on Ganesha, his resolve, and Avidya emerging from his body.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Mudgala speaks. Brahma meditates on Ganesha mentally, resolves to create, and Avidya emerges from Vidhi/Brahma’s body. Do not substitute a mind-born creation.

verses.source_sanskrit:
सा पञ्चधा ततो भिन्ना स्वयं जाता प्रजापते ।
तां दृष्ट्वा विस्मितो ब्रह्मा मनसा दुःखितोऽभवत् ॥२॥
verses.text: ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಯೇ, ಅನಂತರ ಆ ಅವಿದ್ಯೆಯು ತಾನಾಗಿಯೇ ಐದು ವಿಧಗಳಾಗಿ ವಿಭಜಿತಳಾದಳು. ಅವಳನ್ನು ಕಂಡ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು ವಿಸ್ಮಿತನಾಗಿ ಮನಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ದುಃಖಿತನಾದನು. ॥೨॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Fivefold self-division, Prajapati’s vocative, Brahma’s astonishment and grief are retained.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Avidya spontaneously becomes fivefold; Prajapati is the vocative; Brahma is both astonished and mentally distressed.

verses.source_sanskrit:
अविद्याभ्रान्तिरूपाऽत्र ह्यनन्तविभवात्मिका ।
रक्ता कृष्णा तथा श्वेतानानाश्चर्यमयी बभौ ॥३॥
verses.text: ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಆ ಅವಿದ್ಯೆಯು ಭ್ರಾಂತಿಸ್ವರೂಪಿಣಿಯಾಗಿ, ಅನಂತ ವೈಭವಾತ್ಮಿಕೆಯಾಗಿ, ಕೆಂಪು, ಕಪ್ಪು ಹಾಗೂ ಬಿಳಿ ವರ್ಣಗಳನ್ನು ತಳೆದು, ನಾನಾ ಆಶ್ಚರ್ಯಗಳಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿದವಳಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸಿದಳು. ॥೩॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
The red, black, and white colours are retained without assigning them to guṇas or another doctrinal category.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Avidya’s delusion-nature, infinite splendour/power and red, black and white colours are preserved without introducing guna identities.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Avidya has the nature of delusion, unlimited power/splendour, red/black/white forms and many wonders. Do not name unprinted gunas.

verses.source_sanskrit:
त्रिविधानां प्रसूतिश्च जगत्त्रयविमोहिनी ।
तया विमोहितं विश्वं भ्रान्तियुक्तं बभूव ह ॥४॥
verses.text: ಮೂರು ವಿಧಗಳ ಜನನಿಯೂ ಮೂರು ಲೋಕಗಳನ್ನು ಮೋಹಗೊಳಿಸುವವಳೂ ಆದ ಅವಳಿಂದ ಮೋಹಿತವಾದ ವಿಶ್ವವು ಭ್ರಾಂತಿಗೊಳಗಾಯಿತು. (ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ: “ಮೂರು ವಿಧಗಳು” ಯಾವುದನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂಬುದು ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಿಲ್ಲ.) ॥೪॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
त्रिविधानां is clearly printed. No explicit noun or referent is supplied for the three kinds; the Kannada preserves that underspecification.

issues.description: The three kinds have no explicit referent in this verse. Literal Kannada retained with a visible caution; no three-guṇa interpretation supplied.

independent_review.rationale: Held from unqualified resolution, but the literal guarded rendering is approved. The three kinds are unspecified in the visible Sanskrit; the Kannada preserves this and includes a parenthetical notice rather than inventing a referent.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Printed त्रिविधानां प्रसूतिश्च is clear: origin/mother of three kinds, whose categories are unspecified. Three worlds and universal delusion must remain distinct.
independent_review.publication_condition: Preserve translation-review and the visible parenthetical Kannada notice; do not promote this to unqualified source-resolved status.

verses.source_sanskrit:
तमो मोहो महामोहः शृणु दक्ष महाद्भुतम् ।
तामिस्रश्चान्धतामिस्रः पञ्चधा जगति स्थिता ॥५॥
verses.text: ದಕ್ಷನೇ, ಈ ಮಹಾದ್ಭುತವನ್ನು ಕೇಳು. ತಮಸ್ಸು, ಮೋಹ, ಮಹಾಮೋಹ, ತಾಮಿಸ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ಅಂಧತಾಮಿಸ್ರ ಎಂಬ ಐದು ವಿಧಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅವಿದ್ಯೆಯು ಜಗತ್ತಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಲೆಗೊಂಡಿದ್ದಾಳೆ. ॥೫॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. All five names are distinct and complete, with Daksha addressed and Avidya’s fivefold presence retained.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Exactly five forms: tamas, moha, mahamoha, tamisra and andhatamisra; Daksha is addressed.

verses.source_sanskrit:
तमोऽज्ञानस्वरूपं यतेन सञ्छादितं जगत् ।
देहस्वार्थसमायुक्तं बभूव भ्रान्तमानसम् ॥६॥
verses.text: ತಮಸ್ಸು ಅಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ವರೂಪವಾಗಿದೆ. ಅದರಿಂದ ಆವೃತವಾದ ಜಗತ್ತು ದೇಹದ ಸ್ವಾರ್ಥದಲ್ಲಿ ತೊಡಗಿ, ಭ್ರಾಂತಿಗೊಂಡ ಮನಸ್ಸುಳ್ಳದ್ದಾಯಿತು. (ಪಾಠಸೂಚನೆ: ಮೂಲದಲ್ಲಿನ “ಯತೇನ” ರೂಪದ ವ್ಯಾಕರಣಾನುಸಂಧಾನಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿದೆ.) ॥೬॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

Enlarged PT85 confirms the printed यतेन. A possible intended division is यत् तेन, but no Sanskrit emendation has been made. The broad statement about ignorance, bodily self-interest, and delusion remains secure; the exact printed construction is unresolved.
The final equivalent notice explicitly says ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿದೆ; independent review accepted this clearer wording without resolving the grammatical question.

issues.description: The enlarged pixels clearly show यतेन, but its exact grammatical division remains unsettled. A visible Kannada notice distinguishes source-form uncertainty from the secure broad sense.

independent_review.rationale: Held from unqualified source-grammar resolution, but the contextual rendering is approved with its visible notice. Printed यतेन is retained in source metadata and ಯತೇನ is accurately shown in the Kannada notice. Ignorance, covering, bodily self-interest and mental delusion remain intact.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Printed यतेन is clear but irregular. Ignorance-nature, covering the world, bodily self-interest and deluded mind are contextually secure. Retain a visible unresolved-source notice; do not silently substitute येन or यत्तेन.
independent_review.publication_condition: Preserve translation-review and the visible parenthetical Kannada notice; do not promote this to unqualified source-resolved status.

verses.source_sanskrit:
मोहः स कामनायुक्तं कर्म नाना विनिर्ममे ।
तेन विश्वं शरीरस्य कुरुते कर्म भोगदम् ॥७॥
verses.text: ಆ ಮೋಹವು ಕಾಮನೆಗಳಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿದ ನಾನಾ ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿತು. ಅದರಿಂದಾಗಿ ಜಗತ್ತು ಶರೀರಕ್ಕೆ ಭೋಗವನ್ನು ನೀಡುವ ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ॥೭॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
कामनायुक्तं modifies the created karmic activity; the Kannada retains desire-laden actions rather than making a new doctrinal assertion.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Desire-associated diverse actions and actions supplying bodily enjoyment retain the source’s agency and causal sequence.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Moha produces diverse desire-associated action; the world performs action that supplies bodily enjoyment. Do not pre-empt verse 8 by calling every act sinful here.

verses.source_sanskrit:
महामोहेन संसृष्टं विकर्म विविधं प्रभो ।
तेन देहस्य भोगार्थं पापानि कुरुते नरः ॥८॥
verses.text: ಪ್ರಭುವೇ, ಮಹಾಮೋಹವು ನಾನಾವಿಧವಾದ ವಿಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಿತು. ಅದರಿಂದ ಮನುಷ್ಯನು ದೇಹದ ಭೋಗಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಪಾಪಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ. ॥೮॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
विकर्म is retained as the technical Kannada term ವಿಕರ್ಮ; the following pāpa clause makes its harmful character explicit.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Technical ವಿಕರ್ಮ is legitimate formal Kannada; the following explicit sins clause supplies its harmful sense. Bodily enjoyment and human agency are preserved.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Mahamoha creates diverse prohibited/wrong action; a person commits sins for bodily enjoyment. Preserve agency and causal chain.

verses.source_sanskrit:
तामिस्रेण फलं सृष्टं रोगदारिद्र्यकादिकम् ।
तेनाऽऽधिव्याधिसंयुक्तमभूद्विश्वं प्रपीडितम् ॥९॥
verses.text: ತಾಮಿಸ್ರದಿಂದ ರೋಗ, ದಾರಿದ್ರ್ಯ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಫಲಗಳು ಉಂಟಾದವು. ಅದರಿಂದ ವಿಶ್ವವು ಆಧಿ-ವ್ಯಾಧಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಒಳಗಾಗಿ ತೀವ್ರವಾಗಿ ಪೀಡಿತವಾಯಿತು. ॥೯॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

Enlarged PT87 visibly has two s-like marks after तेना. The source_sanskrit field retains the tentative draft normalization to two avagrahas; this is not a verified correction of the typography. The intended आधि–व्याधि expression and meaning of mental/bodily affliction are secure.

source_typography_issues.description: The two s-like printed marks cannot be certified as avagrahas. Tentative normalization only; this typographic uncertainty does not prevent the secure आधि–व्याधि translation.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted semantically. Disease, poverty and oppressive ಆಧಿ-ವ್ಯಾಧಿ are accurately rendered. The two s-like source marks remain explicitly unverified in separate typography metadata; this approval does not certify the normalized double avagraha.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Tamisra produces fruits including disease and poverty; mental and bodily affliction oppress the world. The two s-shaped marks after तेना remain typographically unresolved; double-avagraha is tentative only.

verses.source_transcription_note: Two s-like printed marks are tentatively represented by avagrahas in source_sanskrit. Their glyph identification remains open in source_typography_issues; this is not a certified exact normalization.

verses.source_sanskrit:
अन्धतामिस्रतो दक्ष नरको यातनात्मकः ।
तेन स्वकर्मदोषेण यातनां बुभुजे जगत् ॥१०॥
verses.text: ದಕ್ಷನೇ, ಅಂಧತಾಮಿಸ್ರದಿಂದ ಯಾತನಾಮಯವಾದ ನರಕವು ಉಂಟಾಯಿತು. ಅದರಿಂದ ಜಗತ್ತು ತನ್ನ ಕರ್ಮದ ದೋಷದಿಂದ ಯಾತನೆಯನ್ನು ಅನುಭವಿಸಿತು. ॥೧೦॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. The torment-filled hell arises from Andhatamisra; suffering remains linked to the world’s own karmic fault.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Andhatamisra gives rise to a torment-filled hell; the world experiences torment due to the fault of its own actions. Preserve स्वकर्मदोषेण.

verses.source_sanskrit:
एषाऽविद्यागणेशानं स्मृत्वा स्वार्थपराऽभवत् ।
ततो ब्रह्मा विनिन्द्यैनां पुनः स्रष्टुं मनो दधे ॥११॥
verses.text: ಈ ಅವಿದ್ಯೆಯು ಗಣೇಶನನ್ನು ಸ್ಮರಿಸಿ ಸ್ವಾರ್ಥಪರಳಾದಳು. ಅನಂತರ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು ಅವಳನ್ನು ನಿಂದಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತೆ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಲು ಸಂಕಲ್ಪಿಸಿದನು. ॥೧೧॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
स्मृत्वा explicitly means having remembered. No negation, forgetfulness, or failure to remember Gaṇeśa has been introduced.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. The crucial positive स्मृत्वा is preserved as ಸ್ಮರಿಸಿ; no negation or doctrinal harmonization is invented. Brahma censures Avidya and resolves to create again.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Pixels read स्मृत्वा, not अस्मृत्वा: Avidya remembers Ganesha and becomes intent upon her own ends. Brahma censures her and resolves to create again. Do not insert negation to harmonize doctrine.

verses.source_sanskrit:
ततस्तस्य शरीरातु चतुःपुत्राः प्रजज्ञिरे ।
सनकश्च महायोगी तथान्यश्च सनन्दनः ॥१२॥
verses.text: ಅನಂತರ ಅವನ ಶರೀರದಿಂದ ನಾಲ್ವರು ಪುತ್ರರು ಜನಿಸಿದರು. ಅವರಲ್ಲಿ ಮಹಾಯೋಗಿಯಾದ ಸನಕನು ಮತ್ತು ಮತ್ತೊಬ್ಬನಾದ ಸನಂದನನು ಇದ್ದರು. (ಪಾಠಸೂಚನೆ: ಮೂಲದಲ್ಲಿನ “ಶರೀರಾತು” ರೂಪದ ವ್ಯಾಕರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿದೆ.) ॥೧೨॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

Enlarged PT88 confirms printed शरीरातु. The meaning from his body is secure in context, but the grammatical form is irregular; no silent change to शरीरात्तु has been made. The enumeration continues in verse 13.
The final equivalent notice explicitly says ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿದೆ; independent review accepted this clearer wording without resolving the grammatical question.

issues.description: Readable printed शरीरातु is grammatically irregular. The context supports from his body, but the exact construction is not silently emended; a short Kannada notice is included.

independent_review.rationale: Held from unqualified source-grammar resolution, but the contextual body-origin/four-sons rendering is approved with its visible notice. Enlarged pixels support शरीरातु with a visible u mark; the Kannada notice accurately gives ಶರೀರಾತು without silently repairing the source.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Pixels read शरीरातु with a visible u mark below ta. Body-origin and four sons are contextually clear, including Sanaka and Sanandana, but the exact source inflection is irregular. Keep a visible notice; do not silently replace by शरीरात् or शरीरात्तु.
independent_review.publication_condition: Preserve translation-review and the visible parenthetical Kannada notice; do not promote this to unqualified source-resolved status.

verses.source_sanskrit:
सनातनोऽपि च सनत्कुमारश्च चतुर्थकः ।
तेषां मातृस्वरूपेण विद्या ज्ञानात्मिका बभौ ॥१३॥
verses.text: ಸನಾತನನೂ ನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯವನಾದ ಸನತ್ಕುಮಾರನೂ ಜನಿಸಿದರು. ಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ವರೂಪಿಣಿಯಾದ ವಿದ್ಯೆಯು ಅವರ ಮಾತೃಸ್ವರೂಪವಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸಿದಳು. ॥೧೩॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
Completes the four sons enumerated in verses 12–13; Vidyā is their mother-form, not an additional son.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Sanatana and fourth Sanatkumara complete the four-son enumeration; knowledge-natured Vidya is their mother-form.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Sanatana and fourth Sanatkumara complete the four sons. Knowledge-natured Vidya shines as their mother; do not substitute Avidya.

verses.source_sanskrit:
बोधरूपां निराकारां साक्षादात्ममयीं पराम् ।
दृष्ट्वा तां हर्षयुक्तोऽभूद्ब्रह्मा सर्वपितामहः ॥१४॥
verses.text: ಬೋಧಸ್ವರೂಪಿಣಿಯೂ ನಿರಾಕಾರಳೂ ಸಾಕ್ಷಾತ್ ಆತ್ಮಮಯಳೂ ಪರಮಸ್ವರೂಪಿಣಿಯೂ ಆದ ಆ ವಿದ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಕಂಡು ಸರ್ವಪಿತಾಮಹನಾದ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು ಹರ್ಷಗೊಂಡನು. ॥೧೪॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. The four descriptions of Vidya and Brahma’s joy are preserved with correct identity and agency.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Vidya is consciousness-natured, formless, directly Self-natured and supreme. Brahma the grandsire is the one delighted upon seeing her.

verses.source_sanskrit:
सहजस्य धरस्तत्र सनकः सम्बभौ सुतः ।
समयोगधरो दक्ष प्रतापी च सनन्दनः ॥१५॥
verses.text: ದಕ್ಷನೇ, ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಸನಕನೆಂಬ ಪುತ್ರನು ಸಹಜವನ್ನು ಧರಿಸಿದವನಾಗಿ ಕಾಣಿಸಿಕೊಂಡನು. ಪ್ರತಾಪಿಯಾದ ಸನಂದನನು ಸಮಯೋಗವನ್ನು ಧರಿಸಿದವನಾಗಿದ್ದನು. ॥೧೫॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
सहज and समयोग are preserved as distinct technical expressions; no additional doctrinal identification is supplied.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Sanaka’s sahaja, Sanandana’s samayoga and power, and Daksha’s vocative remain distinct. The restrained technical Kannada avoids an unsupported doctrinal gloss.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Sanaka bears sahaja; Sanandana bears samayoga and is powerful. Daksha is addressed. Do not import an unprinted doctrinal system or normalize samayoga to a different yoga term.

verses.source_sanskrit:
ज्ञानयोगमयो योगी सनातन इति स्मृतः ।
कर्मयोगस्वरूपः सनत्कुमारः स आबभौ ॥१६॥
verses.text: ಜ್ಞಾನಯೋಗಮಯನಾದ ಯೋಗಿಯು ಸನಾತನನೆಂದು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧನಾಗಿದ್ದನು. ಸನತ್ಕುಮಾರನು ಕರ್ಮಯೋಗಸ್ವರೂಪನಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಿಸಿದನು. ॥೧೬॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Knowledge-yoga is assigned to Sanatana and action-yoga to Sanatkumara, with formal narrative grammar.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Sanatana is knowledge-yoga-natured; Sanatkumara is action-yoga-natured. Keep the two assignments distinct.

verses.source_sanskrit:
तान् दृष्ट्वा हर्षसंयुक्त उवाच जगदीश्वरः ।
स्मृत्वाऽसृजत संसृष्टिं गणेशं तैः कृतं तथा ॥१७॥
verses.text: ಅವರನ್ನು ಕಂಡು ಹರ್ಷಗೊಂಡ ಜಗದೀಶ್ವರನಾದ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು, “ಗಣೇಶನನ್ನು ಸ್ಮರಿಸಿ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ರಚಿಸಿರಿ” ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ಅವರೂ ಹಾಗೆಯೇ ಮಾಡಿದರು. (ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ: ಮೂಲದಲ್ಲಿನ “ಸ್ಮೃತ್ವಾಽಸೃಜತ” ರೂಪವು ವ್ಯಾಕರಣದ ದೃಷ್ಟಿಯಿಂದ ಸಂದಿಗ್ಧವಾಗಿದೆ; ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಆದೇಶದ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ಸಂದರ್ಭಾನುಸಾರ ನೀಡಲಾಗಿದೆ.) ॥೧೭॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

The verse begins with उवाच and ends with तैः कृतं तथा. Those surrounding clauses support contextual instruction and compliance. The printed स्मृत्वाऽसृजत, however, does not cleanly give the expected plural imperative; the proposed Kannada speech is expressly flagged, not presented as a settled correction.

issues.source_excerpt: स्मृत्वाऽसृजत संसृष्टिं गणेशं तैः कृतं तथा
issues.description: Contextual instruction and compliance is proposed from उवाच and तैः कृतं तथा, but स्मृत्वाऽसृजत is syntactically irregular. Visible Kannada uncertainty retained; no repaired Sanskrit is substituted.

independent_review.rationale: Held from unqualified syntactic resolution, but the expressly contextual instruction/compliance rendering is approved. The parenthetical Kannada notice correctly identifies ಸ್ಮೃತ್ವಾಽಸೃಜತ and states that the imperative sense is supplied from context. No emended Sanskrit is substituted.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Pixels read स्मृत्वाऽसृजत; the construction is irregular. Brahma’s speaking and तैः कृतं तथा support a contextual instruction to remember Ganesha and create, followed by compliance. Any such rendering must carry a visible note and cannot claim a settled grammatical emendation.
independent_review.publication_condition: Preserve translation-review and the visible parenthetical Kannada notice; do not promote this to unqualified source-resolved status.

verses.source_sanskrit:
नानाविधं योगमार्गं ससृजुस्ते महौजसः ।
तं दृष्ट्वा नाभ्यनन्दत्स ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच तान् पुनः ॥१८॥
verses.text: ಆ ಮಹಾತೇಜಸ್ವಿಗಳು ನಾನಾವಿಧವಾದ ಯೋಗಮಾರ್ಗವನ್ನು ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಿದರು. ಅದನ್ನು ಕಂಡ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು ಸಂತೋಷಪಡಲಿಲ್ಲ; ಮತ್ತೆ ಅವರಿಗೆ ಹೇಳಿದನು. ॥೧೮॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
नाभ्यनन्दत् is preserved as did not rejoice.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. The sons create varied yoga paths; Brahma’s failure to rejoice and his renewed address are retained, including the source negation.
independent_review.independent_source_check: The sons create diverse yoga paths. Brahma does not approve and speaks to them again; retain नाभ्यनन्दत् negation.

verses.source_sanskrit:
अलं योगमयीं सृष्टिं मा कुरुध्वं महौजसः ।
तथेति ते महाभागा ऊचुस्तं संस्थिता बभुः ॥१९॥
verses.text: “ಮಹಾತೇಜಸ್ವಿಗಳೇ, ಸಾಕು! ಯೋಗಮಯವಾದ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಮಾಡಬೇಡಿರಿ.” ಆ ಮಹಾಭಾಗರು ಅವನಿಗೆ “ಹಾಗೆಯೇ ಆಗಲಿ” ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿ ನಿಂತರು. ॥೧೯॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
The explicit prohibition मा कुरुध्वं is preserved. Enlarged PT90 confirms ऊचुस्तं. Their response and subsequent standing/remaining are retained.

issues.description: The enlarged actual source pixels confirm ऊचुस्तं, not the earlier erroneous reading. Kannada preserves they said to him.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. The prohibition, the sons’ assent and their standing/remaining are preserved. Enlarged pixels independently confirm ऊचुस्तं, supporting they said to him.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Brahma says enough and forbids yoga-natured creation. Pixels read ऊचुस्तं: they say तथेति / so be it and remain/stay. Do not imply that they then create a different physical universe.

verses.source_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मा ज्ञानमयीं सृष्टिं ततो दृष्ट्वा चुकोप ह ।
कोपात्तस्य ललाटाद्वै शम्भुः पुत्रो बभूव ह ॥२०॥
verses.text: ಅನಂತರ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು ಜ್ಞಾನಮಯವಾದ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಕಂಡು ಕೋಪಗೊಂಡನು. ಆ ಕೋಪದಿಂದ ಅವನ ಲಲಾಟದಿಂದ ಶಂಭುವು ಪುತ್ರನಾಗಿ ಜನಿಸಿದನು. ॥೨೦॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Knowledge-natured creation, Brahma’s anger, and Shambhu’s birth as his son from his forehead are retained.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Brahma sees knowledge-natured creation and becomes angry. Shambhu is born as his son from his forehead because of this anger.

verses.source_sanskrit:
तुष्टाव तेजसा दीप्तं पञ्चवक्त्रधरं प्रभुम् ।
त्रिनेत्रं दशबाहुं तं चन्द्ररेखाविभूषितम् ॥२१॥
verses.text: ತೇಜಸ್ಸಿನಿಂದ ದೀಪ್ತನಾದ, ಐದು ಮುಖಗಳನ್ನು ಧರಿಸಿದ, ಮೂರು ನೇತ್ರಗಳೂ ಹತ್ತು ಭುಜಗಳೂ ಉಳ್ಳ, ಚಂದ್ರರೇಖೆಯಿಂದ ಅಲಂಕೃತನಾದ ಆ ಪ್ರಭುವನ್ನು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನು ಸ್ತುತಿಸಿದನು. ॥೨೧॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

Enlarged PT90 clearly confirms तुष्टाव, meaning praised. Brahmā is the inherited narrative subject. Verses 21–22 describe Śambhu and the act of praise; they are not a directly quoted hymn and are translated as narrative. Five faces, three eyes, and ten arms are preserved.

issues.description: Enlarged source confirms praised; translated as narrative with Brahmā as inherited subject, not mistaken for a direct hymn.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Enlarged तुष्टाव is translated as Brahma praised. Five faces, three eyes, ten arms, radiance and crescent are all retained. Narrative classification is correct.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Pixels unambiguously read तुष्टाव: Brahma praises the Lord, described as radiant, five-faced, three-eyed, ten-armed and crescent-adorned. This is narration of praise, not the words of a prayer.

verses.source_sanskrit:
अर्धनारीनरं प्राज्ञं त्रिशूलादिसुचिह्नितम् ।
जटाधरं महाकायं व्याघ्रेभाजिनधारकम् ॥२२॥
verses.text: ಆ ಶಂಭುವು ಅರ್ಧಸ್ತ್ರೀ-ಅರ್ಧಪುರುಷಸ್ವರೂಪನೂ ಪ್ರಾಜ್ಞನೂ, ತ್ರಿಶೂಲ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಚಿಹ್ನೆಗಳಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿದವನೂ, ಜಟಾಧಾರಿಯೂ ಮಹಾಕಾಯನೂ, ಹುಲಿ ಹಾಗೂ ಆನೆಯ ಚರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಧರಿಸಿದವನೂ ಆಗಿದ್ದನು. ॥೨೨॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

Enlarged PT91 confirms व्याघ्रेभाजिनधारकम्. Compound interpreted as व्याघ्र + इभ + अजिन: tiger and elephant skins, both retained. Verse 22 continues the description in verse 21; it is not a direct prayer.

issues.description: Enlarged pixels support the compound. Both tiger and elephant skins are retained.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted after the requested refinement was incorporated. Initial ಆ ಶಂಭುವು explicitly identifies the bearer of the attributes and prevents ambiguity after the previous verse’s Brahma subject. Half-female/half-male form, wisdom, emblems, matted hair, great body, and both tiger and elephant skins are retained.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Description continues: half-woman/half-man, wise, marked by trident and other emblems, matted hair, great body. व्याघ्रेभाजिनधारकम् = व्याघ्र + इभ + अजिन supports both tiger and elephant skins.

verses.source_sanskrit:
सहसा जातमात्रेण रुदितं शङ्करेण च ।
तं ब्रह्मा सान्त्वयामास किं रोदिषि वृषध्वज ॥२३॥

notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Newborn Shankara’s immediate crying, Brahma’s consolation and the question with bull-bannered vocative are accurate.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Newborn Shankara cries; Brahma consoles him and asks why he cries, addressing him as bull-bannered. Preserve newborn timing and speaker.

verses.source_sanskrit:
ब्रह्माणमवदद्बालः स्थानं देहि पितः प्रभो ।
मह्यं नामानि सर्वेश कार्यं कथय विस्तरात् ॥२४॥
verses.text: ಆ ಬಾಲಕನು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಗೆ, “ತಂದೆಯೇ, ಪ್ರಭುವೇ, ನನಗೆ ಸ್ಥಾನವನ್ನೂ ನಾಮಗಳನ್ನೂ ನೀಡು. ಸರ್ವೇಶನೇ, ನಾನು ಮಾಡಬೇಕಾದ ಕಾರ್ಯವನ್ನು ವಿಸ್ತಾರವಾಗಿ ತಿಳಿಸು” ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಿದನು. ॥೨೪॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.
नामानि is plural, preserved as ನಾಮಗಳು. This is a spoken request within the narrative, not a hymn.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. The child addresses Brahma, requests an abode and names in the plural, and asks for his work to be detailed. This remains narrative speech rather than hymn transliteration.
independent_review.independent_source_check: The child addresses Brahma as father/lord, asks for an abode and names in the plural, and requests his work to be told in detail.

verses.source_sanskrit:
तं प्रत्युवाच धाता स रोदनाद्रुद्रसंज्ञितः ।
शिव सर्वसुखाधारस्त्वं जातोऽसि महेश्वर ॥२५॥
verses.text: ಆ ಧಾತನು ಅವನಿಗೆ ಉತ್ತರಿಸಿದನು: “ಮಹೇಶ್ವರನೇ, ನೀನು ಅತ್ತುದರಿಂದ ರುದ್ರನೆಂಬ ಹೆಸರನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿರುವೆ. ಶಿವನೇ, ನೀನು ಸಕಲ ಸುಖಗಳಿಗೂ ಆಧಾರನಾಗಿ ಜನಿಸಿರುವೆ.” ॥೨೫॥
notes: Translated from all nine original Sanskrit-only page crops after direct visual inspection; disputed forms checked in enlarged images. No PDF, modern English, or other edition used.

रुद्रसंज्ञितः is explicitly connected to रोदनात्, crying. शिव and महेश्वर are vocatives; no invented sequential conferral of those names is added. Chapter continues beyond this bounded batch; no closing colophon is supplied.

independent_review.rationale: Accepted. Crying accounts for the Rudra designation; Shiva and Maheshvara are retained as vocatives, and support of all happiness is preserved. Moving a vocative within the Kannada speech does not change its function.
independent_review.independent_source_check: Brahma replies that crying accounts for the Rudra designation. Shiva and Maheshvara are addresses; preserve being born as support of all happiness. This is not a chapter ending.
